## Findings

### KIS-001 · Low · P3 · CONFIRMED (conf 95)
**`proposeBehavior` is dead configuration whose comment documents an interceptor that does not exist**

`apps/mobile/src/features/WalletConnect/Wallet/walletKitE2eState.ts:24-25` (type), **`:72-77`** (field + doc), `:86` (default)
Also at: `apps/mobile/src/features/WalletConnect/Wallet/__tests__/walletKitE2eState.test.ts:13`

The doc block states the field *"Drives the e2e fetch interceptor for CGW's `/propose` endpoint: `'live'` → passthrough to the real (staging) gateway, `'fail500'` → synthetic 500"*. No such interceptor exists. A repo-wide search returns four hits for `proposeBehavior` — the type, the field, the default, and a test asserting the default. `apps/mobile/src/platform/fetch.ts` (the app's real fetch wrapper) has no e2e branch; nothing under `apps/mobile/src/tests/e2e-maestro/` reads it; no TestCtrls button sets it.

**Why it matters:** the comment is a trap, not just clutter. Whoever writes the CGW-failure flow will set `proposeBehavior: 'fail500'` as documented and get a live passthrough to staging — a test that looks like it exercises the failure path and does not.

**Origin is stated but does not resolve it.** The commit message says *"Also adds proposeBehavior to drive the CGW /propose fetch interceptor"* — so this is deliberate staging, which is why impact stays I1. Intent is not implementation.

**Cross-reference (conventions):** `git log --follow` on this file shows only two commits ever touched it. The prior one (`40eeaf354`) landed `pairBehavior`, `forceNativeWalletConnect`, `sessions` and `rejectSessionCalled` **together with their consumers in the same diff**. This commit follows that pattern for `lastRequestResponse` and breaks it for `proposeBehavior` — an inconsistency inside a single diff.

**Recommendation:** drop the three lines and re-add them with the interceptor, or keep them and change the doc to future tense with a `TODO` naming the follow-up.

### KIS-002 · Low · P3 · CONFIRMED (conf 90)
**Two comments name a component and test-ids that exist nowhere**

`apps/mobile/src/features/WalletConnect/Wallet/walletKit.e2e.ts:65` — `// Records what the app would deliver to the dApp; WcResponseIndicator surfaces it to Maestro.`
`apps/mobile/src/features/WalletConnect/Wallet/walletKitE2eState.ts:66-68` — `* Side-channel surfaced by WcResponseIndicator (error-code / safeTxHash-match test-ids)`

No `WcResponseIndicator` exists in the repo, and no testID for an error code or a safeTxHash match exists. Searching `Indicator` across `apps/mobile/src/features/WalletConnect` returns only RN's `ActivityIndicator` and bottom-sheet `handleIndicatorStyle`.

**What makes it a finding rather than a nit:** the sibling comment eleven lines above, at `walletKitE2eState.ts:60-62`, uses the identical present-tense documentary style for `rejectSessionCalled` and is *true* — `e2e-wc-reject-called` is rendered at `TestCtrls.e2e.tsx:116` and asserted at `apps/mobile/e2e/tests/walletconnect-dapps/pair-proposal-reject.yml:35`. A reader has no way to tell the true one from the aspirational one.

**Consequence in practice:** `lastRequestResponse` is currently written by the fake and read by nothing except its own unit tests, so the stated purpose — *"so tx-request flows can assert exactly what was delivered"* — is not yet achievable.

**Recommendation:** mark both comments as planned (`will be surfaced by`), or land the indicator.

### KIS-003 · Nit · CONTESTED (conf 60) — refuter WEAKENED
**Hand-rolled `JsonRpcResponseLike`, with a justification that is not accurate**

`apps/mobile/src/features/WalletConnect/Wallet/walletKit.e2e.ts:54-56`, cast at `:123`

The comment says the local type *"avoids depending on `@walletconnect/jsonrpc-types` directly"*. `@walletconnect/jsonrpc-utils` is already a declared dependency (`apps/mobile/package.json:88`) and already imported by production code at `walletKitListeners.ts:2` for `formatJsonRpcResult`/`formatJsonRpcError`, so the response type is derivable at zero dependency cost — e.g. `ReturnType<typeof formatJsonRpcResult> | ReturnType<typeof formatJsonRpcError>`.

**Refuter's mitigation (accepted):** `getWalletKit(): Promise<IWalletKit>` (`:125`) means every call site — including the two new tests — is type-checked against the real SDK signature, not against the local type. Only the fake's read side escapes checking, and it reads a minimal duck-typed subset (`response.id`, `'result' in response`, `response.error`) that any conforming value satisfies. Corrected to I1 × L1 → Nit. The inaccurate justification is the part that remains.

### TST-001 · Nit · unadjudicated
**No test pins the last-write-wins semantics the field's name promises**

`apps/mobile/src/features/WalletConnect/Wallet/__tests__/walletKit.e2e.test.ts:43-69`

Both new tests call `respondSessionRequest` exactly once. Nothing asserts that a second call overwrites the first — which is the whole contract of a field named `lastRequestResponse`, and the thing any future Maestro assertion depends on. Worth knowing when that consumer arrives: a single flow can produce several responses on one topic (`walletKitListeners.ts:209` responds to `wallet_getCallsStatus`, and `:89` responds with the tx result), so "last" and "the one I care about" are not always the same response.

### DRY-001 · Nit · CONTESTED — refuter WEAKENED
**Topic literal hardcoded where the exported constant is the file's own pattern**

`apps/mobile/src/features/WalletConnect/Wallet/__tests__/walletKit.e2e.test.ts:48` and `:62` use `'e2e-session-topic'`, while `E2E_SESSION_TOPIC` is exported for this at `walletKitE2eState.ts:16` and imported by every other consumer, including the sibling test at `walletConnectDappsSetup.test.ts:11`. The same test file already prefers `APPROVED_SESSION.topic` at `:31` and `:39`.

**Refuter's mitigation (accepted):** the fake's `respondSessionRequest` (`walletKit.e2e.ts:66-76`) never looks the topic up against anything — it echoes the caller's string — so the value cannot drift out of sync in a way that breaks these assertions. Readability only. Corrected to I1 × L1 → Nit.
